concept: SearchInput is the Input well with a printed search mark at its start and a Clear key at its end. The key shows only when there is text to clear, and it is a printed word on a 44px strip so nobody has to guess what a small cross does. Enter searches and Escape clears, the way a dial on a radio only does one thing per turn.
family_difference: SearchInput adds a printed search mark, a Clear key that appears with text, Enter to search, Escape to clear, and an optional search landmark and results count.

default_to_avoid.pattern: search input: a pill with a magnifier inside and a small grey cross that appears on hover
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tiny cross is under the touch size, is told apart by shape alone and hides until hover, while a printed word on a 44px strip is found by everyone.

references.source: system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): the printed word beside the scale names what each part does

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The well is surface.sunken with elevation.well, as in Input, so the search field reads as cut into the body.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The Clear key is as tall as the well and runs over its hairline, so the strip is a full 44px target.
The Clear key fades in when text arrives and out when it goes, and nothing else in the field moves.

options.name: round raised cap with a cross, set inside the well
printed word key as a divided strip at the end of the well
raised search key beside the well, bare cross for clear

variants.reason: B keeps the key's meaning in a word that Thai or German can replace and holds a 44px strip without a cap inside a recess. A puts a raised cap inside a recess and shrinks it to 30px of visible target; C needs a second key and prints a bare cross at secondary ink that is hard to see.

root.why: The field stacks its label, well and messages in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight and is the field's accessible name, which a placeholder cannot be.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light, shade on its top-left inner edge, so the person sees where the query goes.

mark.why: A printed search mark at the start tells the field's purpose at a glance, and it is hidden from assistive tech because the label already says it.

field.why: Typed text is primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

clear.why: The Clear key is a printed word on a strip as tall as the well, so the target is 44px and the meaning is in words, not a small cross.

hint.why: The hint is secondary ink in the caption size under the well, and the field is described by it.

error.why: The error is critical red with a glyph and words, never orange and never colour alone.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means invalid is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

md.why: The default well and Clear strip are 44px tall, the smallest target that every part in dial keeps for a finger.

lg.why: A 52px well and Clear strip with larger text for the main field of a phone sheet held in one hand.

focus-within.why: The well shows the same dark ring as every part when the field holds the keyboard focus.

data-state=open.why: The Clear key enters from @starting-style at zero opacity when text arrives, a state change that fades in over motion.release.

hover.why: Hover only darkens the key's ink a step, because a real key does not rise when you approach it.

focus-visible.why: The Clear key shows the same dark ring as every part when the keyboard reaches it.

active.why: A pressed key goes to full primary ink, so the press is seen as the word darkens under the finger.

data-state=closing.why: When the text goes the key fades out over motion.exit, and the pointer passes through it so the field never catches a stray tap.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and fades to half, so it reads as not taking input right now.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion the Clear key only fades on motion.hover, which the tokens keep.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well and the key's divider keep a real border and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.

opacity.why: The Clear key arriving or leaving is a state change, so it fades in over motion.release and out over motion.exit (D-008).

color.why: The key's ink darkens a step over motion.hover when the pointer arrives, the only response a key gives to hover.
